The default agents reader is shared with other hosts; selecting Kilo placement is not exclusive visibility. Project native skills take precedence over global; compatibility-directory duplicate precedence is not established.

skills.paths adds configured readers and skills.urls adds remote acquisition with trust constraints; neither is expanded or modified. No remote fetching, host config migration or enablement is performed.

New-platform mode-specific stores are not used. Legacy extension, desktop, JetBrains, cloud and remote variants remain unverified or excluded.

Name Matching Rule and Common Errors require folder/name agreement, while Skill Not Loading says otherwise. This installer retains stricter general-spec agreement; exact host acceptance remains unverified. No additional reserved local name is established.

Skill Locations provides Mac/Linux and Windows home examples. Native resolver/copy tests do not establish installed host versions or discovery/activation. Host embedded-shell behavior is not exercised.

Current native user skills move with KIMI_CODE_HOME; the independent .agents reader stays under OS home. The caller must supply that home explicitly even when native storage is overridden.
The host defines project root by its nearest .git ancestor. This resolver takes the selected root explicitly, does not search ancestors and does not infer application workspace semantics.

Project takes precedence over User, Extra and Built-in. extra_skill_dirs and host built-ins are not enumerated or modified; same-tier duplicate precedence and additional reserved local names remain unverified.

Only canonical directory-form skills are installed; flat Markdown skills, host prompt/flow invocation, placeholders, built-ins and activation are separate capabilities. Stricter general metadata/folder matching remains required.

Getting started, Installation (https://moonshotai.github.io/kimi-code/en/guides/getting-started.html), reviewed 2026-10-16, documents macOS/Linux and Windows with Git Bash. No host or shell prerequisite was installed or launched.
IDE/ACP, browser/remote, archived Python and Rust-agent variants are separate unverified or excluded capabilities. Successful native library copying does not validate real-host discovery.

CLI native defaults are .junie/skills with separate .agents readers. Project overrides user for duplicate native names; compatibility duplicate precedence remains unverified.

Project .agents skills require a trusted project. Default roots can be disabled via --skill-default-locations, JUNIE_SKILL_DEFAULT_LOCATIONS or configuration. Additional skill locations, extension/built-in skills and enabled state are not modeled or modified.

Environment variables, Configuration files (https://junie.jetbrains.com/docs/environment-variables.html; updated 2026-10-15, reviewed 2026-10-16) names JUNIE_HOME as home storage, but the reviewed skills sections do not establish its exact replacement skill roots. JUNIE_HOME relocation remains unverified and is not interpreted as a skills write override.

Config documentation (https://junie.jetbrains.com/docs/junie-cli-configuration.html; reviewed 2026-10-16), Project trust, describes temporary project storage for untrusted interactive projects. This installer does not grant trust or target transient host-managed storage.

The skills introduction mentions IDE support, but its path sections specify CLI. AI Assistant 2026.2 Agents (https://www.jetbrains.com/help/ai-assistant/agents.html; updated 2026-10-07, reviewed 2026-10-16) does not list native Junie skills as supported. Native IDE/plugin and CLI-via-ACP discovery remain separate version/surface gaps; no IDE target is enabled.
Cursor/Claude/Codex directories are described as import candidates, not default readable roots. No import/migration is performed and no fork path or state-home override is inherited.

Only canonical directory-form skills with general-spec metadata are installed. The host optional-description convenience does not weaken validation. No additional reserved local name or minimum skills version is established.
Skill location provides macOS/Linux and Windows home examples. Native copying does not prove host discovery, activation, trust or a validated installed version.
